title: Unified Inference: Q1 Product Overview, PRD, Design Spec, Roadmap & Pricing - 2026-03-04
author: Sofia Ramirez
body:
Overview

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD, key requirements, high-level design, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for the Unified Inference initiative (Q1 2026). Unified Inference is Redwood's effort to provide a single, consistent developer experience and runtime that spans Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments with a focus on predictable latency, cost control, and operational tooling.

Goals

- Provide a single API and configuration surface that guarantees behavioral parity across deployment modes.
- Reduce per-token unit cost by 10-25% for common web-app workloads via smarter routing, batching and KV caching.
- Ship first-class rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback) tied to model versioning and per-route SLOs.
- Offer straightforward pricing and packaging that maps to small startup, scale, and enterprise buyer needs.

Scope

In-scope for Q1 2026 release:
- Unified API surface (text generation, chat, embeddings, streaming) with stable contract and backward-compatible additions.
- Smart routing engine with simple rule language supporting latency/cost/region precedence, plus automatic fallback to compatible variants.
- Default caching and batching profiles per route with per-customer overrides.
- Rollout primitives in Redwood Console (canary, percentage, auto-fallback).
- Pricing & packaging updates for Hosted API tiers and Dedicated reserved capacity proposals.

Out of scope: fine-grained per-token billing model changes, on-prem operator UX revamp (to be planned Q2), multi-cloud private control plane (explore in Q3).

Product Requirements (PRD)

1) Functional Requirements
  1.1 Unified API parity
    - The REST/SDK endpoints must support identical request/response schemas across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private when using the same model version.
    - Streaming must follow the same chunking semantics and error codes.
  1.2 Smart routing
    - Operators must be able to specify rules with the following attributes: priority, condition (latency/cost/region/tier), target model(s), fallback targets.
    - The system must route <1% of traffic to fallback model variants under normal capacity.
  1.3 Batching & caching profiles
    - Offer three default profiles: low-latency (min-batch=1, max-delay=2ms), balanced (min-batch=4, max-delay=8ms), high-throughput (min-batch=16, max-delay=30ms).
    - Per-customer overrides via configuration in Console and API.
  1.4 Rollouts and safety
    - Canary launch: configurable by percentage and interval with automatic rollback on SLO breach or quality regression threshold.
    - Quality regressions use customer-provided prompt-set evals and Redwood's integrated regression harness.

2) Non-functional Requirements
  - Latency SLOs: P95 generation latency for short prompts (<128 tokens) must be <= 150ms for Hosted Standard tier in us-east-1.
  - Availability: 99.9% uptime for Hosted critical paths (API gateway to response start).
  - Observability: Per-route token breakdown, KV cache hit ratio, batching statistics, and model-switch counts surfaced in Console with 7-day default retention.
  - Security: Must honor per-customer KMS keys for Private deployments and redact secrets in logs.

3) Acceptance Criteria
  - Integration test harness runs end-to-end Signed-off tests for Hosted and Dedicated with a synthetic workload and meets latency and availability targets for 7-day run.
  - Regression harness detects semantic quality regressions on designated prompt sets and triggers an alert when delta exceeds configured threshold.

Design Spec (high-level)

1) Architecture overview
- Client -> Redwood API Gateway -> Routing Service -> Model Serving Pool(s) -> Response Assembly/Streaming -> Client.
- Routing Service consults policy cache (local LRU + config store) and capacity plane to choose target pool.
- Model Serving Pools are labeled by model-version/quantization/profile/region and expose health, capacity, and average latency metrics.

2) Routing policy language (example)
- Syntax (JSON/DSL):
  {
    "priority": 10,
    "condition": "region == 'eu-west-1' && latency_target <= 100",
    "targets": ["gptx-std-8bit", "gptx-fast-6bit"],
    "fallback": "gptx-compat-4bit"
  }

- Policies are evaluated in priority order; the first matching policy wins.

3) Caching & batching implementation details
- KV cache: per-model LRU store with a configurable global memory cap (default 16GB per GPU). Cache keys are (model_version, prompt_prefix_hash).
- Batching: continuous batching queue per GPU with adaptive timeouts based on observed throughput. Profiles (low-latency/balanced/high-throughput) map to min-batch and max-delay knobs.

4) Console UX (overview)
- New route configuration UI: section to set routing policies, batching profile, rollout strategy, and per-route SLOs.
- Rollout visualization: live percentage, error rate, latency delta, and quality regression score.

Migration/Compatibility Notes

- Backwards compatibility: existing endpoints remain valid. New optional parameters (routing_policy_id, batching_profile) default to "system" behavior.
- Migration path for customers:
  1. Create a route and test with canary=1% using Unified Inference.
  2. Monitor Console for P95 and cache-hit ratio for 48 hours.
  3. Gradually increase traffic to 25% -> 50% -> 100% while watching auto-fallback metrics.

API Examples

1) Create route (curl):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "customer-support-rerank",
    "model": "gptx-std-8bit",
    "routing_policy": "latency-first-eu",
    "batching_profile": "balanced",
    "rollout": {"strategy": "canary", "percentage": 1}
  }'

2) Sample generation (Python SDK):

# python pseudo-code
resp = redwood.responses.create(
  model="gptx-std-8bit",
  input="Summarize the following conversation:",
  streaming=True,
  timeout=30
)

Roadmap & Themes (Q2 2026 planning horizon)

Milestones:

| Milestone | Delivery window | Owner |
|---|---:|---|
| Unified API GA (parity tests + docs) | 2026-03-04 | API/Docs Team |
| Smart routing v1 (policy engine + Console) | 2026-04-15 | Serving Runtime Team |
| Batching & caching optimizations | 2026-05-01 | Runtime/Infra Team |
| Dedicated capacity packaging | 2026-05-20 | Product/Commercial |
| Private deployment validation & enterprise checklist | 2026-06-10 | Private Deployments Team |

Themes for next two quarters:
- Developer productivity: better defaults and quickstarts to reduce time-to-value.
- Cost transparency: per-route cost attribution and recommended quantization profiles.
- Reliability: multi-variant fallbacks and degraded-mode behavior testing.

Pricing & Packaging Notes

Objective: Simplify pricing so customers can quickly evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key principles: predictable unit economics, clear upgrade path, and optional add-ons for enterprise needs.

Proposed Hosted Tiers (summary):
- Starter (self-serve): $0/mo + $0.0009 per token (generation), 30-day retention of observability, community support.
- Standard: $99/mo + $0.0006 per token, 7-day observability retention, 99.9% uptime, email support.
- Pro: $999/mo + $0.00035 per token, 30-day observability, SSO, 24/7 support, access to advanced batching/caching presets.

Dedicated packaging (summary):
- Small: 4 GPUs reserved, baseline throughput X, $Y/mo commit (example pricing in sales docs).
- Medium: 16 GPUs reserved, SLA-backed throughput guarantees, enterprise add-ons for longer retention and compliance.
- Enterprise/Private: custom quoting; includes Private control plane, KMS-integrations, audit logging at scale.

Add-on pricing notes:
- Extended observability retention: $200/mo per extra 30 days up to 365 days.
- Model evaluation and regression harness as a managed service: one-time setup fee + monthly retainer.

Billing & Migration guidance for customers:
- Customers on older per-token plans will see their rates grandfathered for 12 months with opt-in to new tiers.
- Dedicated contracts include annual true-up clauses for used capacity. Sales should reference the pricing playbook for regional price adjustments.

Release Notes (this release - 2026-03-04)

Summary:
- GA: Unified API parity across Hosted and Dedicated for text generation, chat, and embeddings.
- New routing policy engine (v0.9) with Console integrations for route configuration and rollouts.
- Default batching & caching profiles introduced and available via API/Console.
- New pricing tiers published for Hosted and preliminary Dedicated packaging.

Notable fixes and changes:
- Fixed: Token accounting mismatch for streaming responses under high concurrency (issue #INF-2143).
- Changed: Default retry policy amended from 3 fast retries to exponential backoff with jitter for model pool failover.
- Deprecated: Legacy batching flag `enable_legacy_batcher` marked deprecated and will be removed in Q3 2026.

Known issues and mitigation:
- Cache warm-up: cold-starts can exhibit higher initial latency for rare prompt prefixes. Mitigation: provide an opt-in pre-warm path in the Console and recommend seed prompt-sets for high-value routes.
- Routing telemetry delay: routing decision metrics may lag by up to 45s in the Console under extreme load; a hotfix is scheduled for 2026-03-20.

Operational runbook (high level)

1) SLO breach (P95 latency > target)
  1) Confirm affected routes via Console (filter by route).
  2) Check model-pool health and capacity metrics. If CPU/GPU saturation > 80%, scale up or shift traffic to lower-cost fallback variants.
  3) Roll back recent policy changes or increase canary thresholds.
  4) Notify on-call and product owner.

2) Quality regression detected (regression harness alert)
  1) Identify the regression prompt-set and compare top-k outputs.
  2) If regression caused by model change, create a rollback token in Console and trigger canary rollback.
  3) Initiate a triage with Applied ML to determine root cause and regression window.

Appendix

A. Example configuration table (Console route fields)

| Field | Type | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| name | string | Route identifier | required |
| model | string | Model version to target | gptx-std-8bit |
| routing_policy | string | Policy id or "system" | system |
| batching_profile | string | one of [low-latency, balanced, high-throughput] | balanced |
| rollout | object | {strategy, percentage, interval} | {"strategy":"instant"} |
